speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis. The clinical picture of sudden, continuous vertigo lasting hours (patient's "3 minutes" is likely an underestimation of the acute episode duration common in this condition) with nausea, vomiting, and no hearing loss or neurological deficits on normal imaging strongly supports a diagnosis of vestibular neuritis, likely viral in origin.
